text: agentOS Context 是面向 DSH Web 与 Desktop 的记忆和知识插件。它通过 DSH Host 注册记忆工具、接受对话提示捕获并在会话步骤中按授权范围检索记忆，也在 Web 界面提供设置页与会话记忆视图。主要能力包括长期记忆召回、记忆管理与关系图谱、文档知识上传和检索。适合希望跨会话保留信息并查询本地资料的 DSH 用户。知识文档解析在本机进行；配置模型服务后，提炼或向量化会使用已配置的服务。

agentOS Context adds long-term memory and document search to DSH. It captures prompts, recalls relevant memories within authorized scopes, and provides a memory settings page and conversation view. Users can upload local documents and search their contents.
想让 DSH 在后续会话里记住重要偏好和决定。
有没有办法按当前问题自动找回相关的旧记忆？
我想在 DSH 里查看和整理已有记忆及其关系。
能不能把本地文档放进知识库，再用自然语言搜索？
I want DSH to remember useful details across sessions.
Can my assistant retrieve relevant memories for each new question?
agentOS Context 的功能「跨会话记忆召回」：收到获准进入模型处理的消息后，插件按会话身份和授权范围搜索记忆，并把有限长度的相关证据附加到本轮上下文。
agentOS Context 的功能「记忆设置与会话视图」：在 DSH 设置区提供记忆配置入口，并在对话视图注册记忆页签，供用户查看记忆内容和工作台。
agentOS Context 的功能「本地文档知识检索」：用户可将支持的文档加入知识库，再通过知识工具搜索相关片段；文档解析在本地完成。

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Introduction：> **Fork notice**: this package is a community fork of the internal `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agentos-context` 0.2.1-rc.5 source, published as `@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context` (MIT). It inlines the DSH 0.2.1 client primitives so the web half loads on the public build, removes deployment-specific gateway defaults and wording, and redesigns the memory graph. Data format, tools and RPC namespaces are unchanged.
description: "Automatic memory, scoped recall, ontology graph, and local document knowledge for DSH Web and Desktop profiles."
kind: "package-bundle"

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · @wilshi/dsh-agentos-context：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Summary：agentOS Context adds automatic long-term memory, scoped recall, a source-backed ontology graph, and a local document knowledge base to a DSH profile. The Web application and DSH Desktop include it by default. Existing OpenContext data remains readable without a destructive migration, while new records use an additive sidecar. Profile maintainers can add or remove the bundle with `dsh plugin`; its ontology is intentionally finite rather than a general OWL reasoner.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Table of Contents：- [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) -----

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Use this package：DSH Web and Desktop already mount this package through `dsh-web-app`. Open **Settings → Memory** to configure capture, recall, embeddings, distillation and retention, or use the Memory workspace for the list, graph, review and knowledge views. The Settings row and Conversation tab follow the active DSH language. A profile that does not include `dsh-web-app` can activate or remove the installed bundle explicitly:

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Use this package：```text
dsh plugin --profile <name> add @wilshi/dsh-agentos-context
dsh plugin --profile <name> remove @wilshi/dsh-agentos-context
```

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Use this package：Adding the bundle mounts the current implementation on the compatibility `dsh-opencontext` Loader row. Official Settings therefore imports the old section into the same namespace and preserves its values. Fields marked volatile apply live without remounting the plugin, but some volatile switches (including automatic capture) are process-local and return to their defaults after a restart; check the persistence semantics rather than assuming every switch is permanent. Explicit Settings values take precedence over environment variables, which only provide defaults when a field was not explicitly configured. The command fails if the installed package does not expose its `dsh.bundle.patch` declaration.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Automatic memory and recall：Automatic human-prompt capture is enabled by default and can be disabled. Accepted prompts are distilled when a configured model is available; a temporary distillation failure retains a low-importance working memory for 24 hours instead of dropping the prompt. Recall searches authorized scopes in `run → agent → workspace → user → app → global` order, keeps run memory inside one Session, and injects only bounded evidence for the accepted user query.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Automatic memory and recall：The 3+1 hierarchy stores working, episodic, semantic and procedural layers independently from memory type. Repeated evidence can reinforce and promote a record; approximate conflicts become review candidates rather than overwriting an established fact. Credential-shaped content is explicitly protected: automatic capture skips prompts that look like keys, tokens or private keys, and explicit save/revise/reinforce returns `SECRET_REJECTED` instead of sending the content to a distillation gateway or writing it into the sidecar. Log redaction covers common GitHub, AWS, GitLab, npm, PEM and Bearer/Basic forms. Ordinary local content remains lossless.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Automatic memory and recall：Workspace scopes such as `local:`, `run:` and `session:` remain available over RPC. `user:`, `agent:` and `app:` identity scopes are limited to the current trusted Session identity or explicitly configured identities; `scopes` and `bootstrap` only expose visible partitions. Legacy integrations can opt into the old behavior with `allowForeignScopeIds=true` (or `AGENTOS_CONTEXT_ALLOW_FOREIGN_SCOPE_IDS`), but this is not recommended for multi-user or remote deployments.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Automatic memory and recall：Searching the compact conversation Memory view is executed by every underlying scope instead of filtering only the recent records already loaded in the browser. The results are merged and ranked back into the aggregate view, so older matching memories remain discoverable without changing the active workspace.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Knowledge and document parsing：Knowledge uploads are explicit. With All scopes selected, the Knowledge view aggregates current and legacy documents while new uploads continue to enter the shared global scope. It can upload, list, search, inspect, reindex and delete text files up to 4 MiB and DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, ODT, ODS, ODP, ODG, RTF or EPUB files up to 25 MiB. Binary extraction runs locally with OCR, attachment extraction and external parser services disabled; only bounded extracted text and source metadata enter the index. Indexing and search use separate default deadlines of 10 minutes and 30 seconds.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Knowledge and document parsing：Lexical retrieval remains available without embedding credentials. When embeddings are configured, the package loads the local SQLite vector extension and combines lexical and semantic results. Model-backed distillation and embedding send selected text and the configured credential only to endpoints in the startup allowlist; remote endpoints must use HTTPS, while plain HTTP is allowed only for loopback addresses or endpoints explicitly listed in OPENCONTEXT_DSH_TRUSTED_GATEWAY_BASES.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Graph, ontology and compatibility：The workbench offers a 2D relationship view and an optional remembered WebGL 3D point-cloud view with orbit, zoom, picking, community folding, active light or dark application colors and a source-backed detail drawer; an unsupported WebGL environment falls back to 2D. Model extraction can propose typed objects and relations, but each relation must quote its source exactly and stays pending until a person confirms it. The aggregate view folds a large graph into one community per memory scope before a person opens a scope, while a single scope uses deterministic relationship communities and retains cross-community edges.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Graph, ontology and compatibility：In Desktop, leaving native fullscreen also closes graph fullscreen when the DOM fullscreen event is absent. DOM fullscreen entry restores the graph after a rapid reentry, and a delayed earlier native exit does not close the active DOM graph. An explicit toggle or Escape exit remains in force when an earlier pending DOM fullscreen entry arrives; that entry is exited rather than restoring graph fullscreen. The CSS-only fullscreen fallback remains dismissible with Escape.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Graph, ontology and compatibility：Legacy OpenContext memories and document references remain read-only inputs and are never rewritten at startup. The package preserves the `dsh-opencontext` settings namespace, reads compatibility identifiers, and keeps callable `oc_*` aliases while presenting `memory_*`, `knowledge_*` and `context_*` names. New revisions, retirements, usage traces and ontology state live in the agentOS Context sidecar; schema-v1 sidecars migrate additively to schema v2.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Graph, ontology and compatibility：If the sidecar or native SQLite dependencies fail to initialize, the plugin stays loaded and reports `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of taking down the whole memory surface; native knowledge dependencies load on demand. Graph statistics distinguish `truncated` (actual clipping) from `depthLimited` (a caller-requested depth boundary), and default nodes are selected by record time. Isolated nodes are merged into an unclustered community instead of producing one community per node. Review transitions are limited to pending → confirmed/rejected; confirmed → rejected is a retraction, and rejected relations cannot be directly confirmed again.
@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Graph, ontology and compatibility：-----

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Understand the implementation：The bundle patch inserts one dual-face Cordis package. Its Host face opens the compatibility backend and sidecar, registers authenticated `agentos-context/v1/*` RPC routes, model tools, the runtime skill and agent lifecycle listeners. Its Client face installs the first-level Memory settings section and workbench views. Browser operations use authenticated Connection RPC instead of legacy raw browser routes. Modal views use package-local UI primitives for focus containment, topmost-only Escape handling and focus restoration, while this package owns their content and layout.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Understand the implementation：Legacy OpenContext storage loads on its first operation, not while importing the plugin for CLI help or schema inspection. Disposing an unused compatibility backend closes any owned document store without loading legacy storage.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Understand the implementation：The sidecar keeps immutable source and memory revisions, typed entities, reviewed relations, temporal validity, idempotency and usage policy in SQLite. The vector index uses the same scope and revision checks, so a stale or unauthorized embedding cannot become a recall result. Existing OpenContext records are projected conservatively and stay in their original database.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Further Exploration：- [Compatibility and operation contract](docs/CONTRACT.md) - [Interaction prototype](prototype/PROTOTYPE.md) - [DSH profile and bundle composition](../../../docs/architecture.md) -----

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · What the model sees：For an accepted human query, the package appends one `agentos-context`-origin user message containing a bounded `<opencontext_evidence>` block. The producer-owned source remains valid in the current Session format. The block labels recalled records as untrusted evidence, escapes record content and ids, and includes only records from scopes authorized for the current Session.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Token effect：Recall adds at most the configured `maxBytes` evidence budget plus its fixed wrapper. No matching record adds no message. The usage tracker records which exact revisions reached a committed request.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · KV Cache effect：The evidence message follows the current human message, so a different query or memory result changes the request suffix without rewriting earlier durable conversation history.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · What the model sees：The package registers descriptive tools including `memory_search`, `memory_save`, `knowledge_search` and `knowledge_document_upload`; older `oc_*` names remain callable aliases. Tool results return bounded structured records or document chunks and never grant authority to recalled text.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Token effect：Tool schemas contribute their fixed definitions to presets that mount this package. Tool calls add only the bounded result selected by the model and the configured per-operation limits.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · KV Cache effect：Stable tool definitions can retain the request prefix cache. A tool result appends new history in the ordinary tool-call position and does not mutate previous messages.

@wilshi/dsh-agentos-context README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- The ontology uses approved finite entity and relationship types; it does not implement arbitrary OWL reasoning, organization-wide authorization, automatic conflict adjudication, review undo, irreversible purge or cross-project sharing.
- Legacy `.doc`, `.xls`, `.ppt` and proprietary `.wps`, `.et`, `.dps` files are not parsed. Save them as OOXML or ODF first. Image-only PDFs require OCR and are rejected when they contain no extractable text.
- Automatic capture writes to the current workspace by default. User, Agent and application scopes require trusted runtime identity or explicit local configuration; an untrusted message cannot manufacture those identities.
- Rolling back to the legacy plugin leaves original records intact but hides sidecar-only writes. A legacy record retired only in the sidecar can therefore reappear after rollback; preserve both databases during evaluation.
- Knowledge uploads are local explicit actions. This package does not crawl folders, synchronize external repositories or perform OCR.
